title: Kenyan Boiled Egg Curry
community: Swahili — popular nationwide with coastal spice influence
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Boiled Egg Curry with Swahili coastal spices — hard-boiled eggs fried until golden then simmered in a richly spiced coconut-tomato sauce with cardamom, cinnamon, and fresh coriander. The coastal elevation of the everyday egg curry — fragrant, rich, and deeply satisfying.
longDesc: This is egg curry elevated with the full Swahili coastal spice palette — whole cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves adding aromatic depth to the tomato base, finished with a generous pour of coconut milk that transforms it into something truly special. The eggs, fried first until golden, develop a slightly crispy exterior that absorbs the coconut sauce beautifully during simmering.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add the peeled hard-boiled eggs and fry for 3—4 minutes, turning, until golden brown all over. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining oil. Add whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves) and fry 30 seconds.
Add onions. Cook until deeply golden — 10 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, curry powder, turmeric, and paprika. Cook for 8—10 minutes until thick.
Pour in coconut milk. Stir gently. Bring to a gentle simmer — do not boil hard.
Add the fried eggs. Spoon sauce over them.
Stir in garam masala and lemon juice.
Scatter coriander and serve with rice.
chefTips: Frying the eggs first creates a golden, lightly crispy exterior that absorbs the coconut curry sauce much better than unfried eggs.
The whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves) at the beginning build the aromatic base of this coastal curry — do not skip them.
Never boil the coconut milk vigorously — it splits.
commonMistakes: Boiling the coconut milk hard — it separates and becomes oily.
Skipping the initial egg frying — the eggs remain smooth and do not absorb the sauce as deeply.

faqs.q: Is this different from KEN092 (Egg Curry)?
faqs.a: Yes — this coastal version adds whole Swahili spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves) for a more aromatic base, and finishes with coconut milk for a richer, creamier sauce. KEN092 is the classic everyday version; this is the celebratory coastal version.

cookingScience: Frying the egg creates micro-fissures and a porous texture on the white's surface through protein contraction and slight dehydration. This porous exterior absorbs the surrounding sauce by capillary action during simmering — creating a far more flavourful egg than one that was simply boiled and added to sauce.
sustainabilityTips: This dish demonstrates how coconut milk can transform affordable eggs into a special meal — sustainability and indulgence together.
reheating: Reheat very gently on stovetop over low heat.
culturalNote: This coastal egg curry reflects the Swahili tradition of elevating simple everyday ingredients with aromatic spices and coconut milk — a culinary philosophy that has shaped the most celebrated dishes of the Kenyan coast for centuries.
regionalVariations: Dry version — coconut milk reduced to a glaze.
